events.body:
The trace settles the route element: no off-route segment was measured (RD-1 ✗), and the GPS record shows 8.5 km actual against 8.5 km optimal, +0.0 km (-0%) [F1]; the fare record agrees that billed distance 8.5 km does not exceed the optimal route [F3]. With no unexempted segment there is nothing for RD-2 to refund, so segment_findings is empty and the distance component of $11.99 contains no excess mileage [F5][RD-1].

The rider's stated grievance — "the fare was higher than I expected … heavy rain, the driver must have taken a longer route" — is answered by the records rather than by the driver's word: the trip ran 22.0 min against a 16.3 min estimate (+5.7 min) [F2], and on this RydeTAXI metered fare that elapsed time was billed as a $5.72 time component on 22.0 min [F5]. RD-2 only refunds unexempted extra mileage, and there is none, so the meter accrual stands [F3][RD-2].

No refund formula is engaged: the trip is a metered RydeTAXI fare (base $3.90 + distance $11.99 (8.50 km) + time $5.72 (22.0 min) + waiting $0.00 + platform $1.47 = $23.08) [F5] at surge 1.0× with no discount [F4]. Nothing in the itemisation is unpublished or unsupported, so FARE-1 yields no refund line [F5][FARE-1].

claims.assertion: There is no off-route segment to complain of: the GPS track shows the actual distance travelled was 8.5 km, exactly equal to the optimal route's 8.5 km (+0.0 km, -0%), so no distance-based detour refund can be calculated for my client.

The billed distance (8.5 km) does not exceed the optimal route distance (8.5 km), so the distance component of $11.99 was charged on exactly the optimal mileage and contains no excess to refund under the detour rules.

The whole of the extra charge my client noticed is explained by time, not by route: the trip took 22.0 min against an estimate of 16.3 min (+5.7 min), and the fare includes a time component of $5.72 for those 22.0 minutes — this is the metered cost of slow traffic, not of a longer route.

The slowness is corroborated by external records rather than by any driver excuse: heavy rain (18.5 mm, thundery showers) plus speed band 3 (20-29 km/h) on both the Pan Island Expressway and Airport Boulevard throughout 17:09-17:47 covers the entire 17:20-17:42 trip window; no traffic incident was recorded (F10), so no segment needed to be avoided.

There is no in-app chat record at all, so no route-change message from the driver was ever put to my client and no consent (general or route-specific) exists in the record; the driver's written statement that he followed the app route is consistent with the GPS figure in F1 and is not contradicted by any system record.

The fare total of $23.08 comprises base $3.90, metered distance $11.99, metered time $5.72, platform $1.47, with no waiting fee, no surge (1.0x), no discount and no unlisted add-on, so there is no undisclosed charge to waive under the fare rules.

The driver's profile shows 1163 trips in 90 days with only 1 dispute and 0 upheld, and my client has 0 disputes in 90 days, so there is no repeated-violation pattern that would justify an account flag; nor does the record support any safety escalation (no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation appears anywhere in the complaint, chat or statement).

weaknesses: My client's expectation of overcharging is factually wrong on the route: F1 and F3 both show 8.5 km actual = 8.5 km optimal, so the driver's denial (F7) is corroborated by the system records and I cannot argue any detour refund.

The fare is a RydeTAXI metered fare, so any extra time spent in rain is chargeable by the meter (F5 time $5.72); my client hoped for a discount for the rain delay, but the policy provides no relief for weather-related slowness, and F11/F8/F9 actually explain why the meter ran higher.

If the case were framed as a detour claim, the outcome would be no_action and the driver's conduct would still be recorded as compliant; the only realistic value in this brief is confirming no overcharge rather than recovering money.

claims.assertion: There is no off-route segment in this trip: the GPS record shows actual distance 8.5 km against an optimal route of 8.5 km, i.e. +0.0 km / -0%, so no detour existed for RD-1 to examine.

The billing is consistent with that same 8.5 km: the fare record confirms billed distance 8.5 km does not exceed the optimal route of 8.5 km, so no extra distance was charged on which any refund could be computed.

The higher-than-expected fare the rider complains of is explained by elapsed time, not by distance: the trip took 22.0 min versus 16.3 min estimated (+5.7 min), and the metered RydeTAXI fare includes time units ($5.72 time component on a 22.0 min trip).

The slow running time is corroborated by conditions on the route the driver actually used: PAN ISLAND EXPRESSWAY and AIRPORT BOULEVARD both recorded speed band 3 (20-29 km/h) throughout 17:09-17:47, overlapping the 17:20-17:42 trip window.
Heavy rain and thundery showers (18.5 mm) during the trip further explain the added 5.7 min of running time, and the ride was charged with no surge multiplier (1.0x).
There is no in-app chat in this case and the rider never named a different route or stop, so there is no rider-requested deviation to weigh and no consent issue arises.

The charge is a metered RydeTAXI fare itemised as base $3.90, distance $11.99 for 8.50 km, time $5.72 for 22.0 min, waiting $0.00 and platform $1.47, totalling $23.08 with no undisclosed add-on, so nothing falls to be refunded under FARE-1.
The driver's account history is not a basis for any account action here: 1 dispute in 90 days with 0 upheld (route 0, no-show 0), so there is no 'repeated' route violation to trigger flag_account.

weaknesses: The rider will point to the +5.7 min over estimate (F2) as proof of something wrong; we must concede the trip was slower than estimated and rely on F8/F9/F11 to attribute it to traffic and rain rather than to the driver.

The recorded optimal route was 8.5 km and equal to actual (F1), but the case file contains no road-name fact tying the driven path to a named road; if the judge treats the meter time component ($5.72, F5) as an overcharge complaint, the dispute turns on duration rather than distance, which is less clean for us.

The traffic evidence shows speed band 3 (20-29 km/h, F8, F9), not band 1 or 2, and F10 records no traffic incident near the route, so RD-4's strict exemptions (a) and (b) are not satisfied on their face - we rely on the conditions as context for the duration, not as a formal exemption.
The fare facts do not break the $5.72 time component into meter waiting units, so we cannot show from a fact id that the time charge exactly matches LTA's 45-second waiting units.

points.response: Conceded — my own brief C1 rests on the same record: F1 shows 8.5 km actual against 8.5 km optimal (+0.0 km), so there is no off-route segment for RD-1 to examine and I withdraw any detour theory.

Accepted as far as it goes: F3 confirms billed distance 8.5 km does not exceed the optimal 8.5 km, so the $11.99 distance component in F5 contains no excess mileage — but that only negates a distance refund under RD-2, it does not show the whole fare was properly earned.

Agreed on the arithmetic and on its effect: F2 (+5.7 min) and F5 ($5.72 time component on 22.0 min) show the extra my client felt was time-based meter accrual, not a longer route, and RD-2 refunds only unexempted extra mileage.

I accept F8 and F9 as accurate conditions on the route used (band 3, 20-29 km/h, 17:09-17:47), but note the driver's own weakness: RD-4(b) requires band 1 or 2 to exempt a segment and F10 records no incident, so these facts explain duration and cannot be used to excuse any deviation — there is none anyway.
F11 and F4 are not in dispute; heavy rain and the absence of surge are simply context, and neither creates nor defeats a refund under RD-4 or FARE-1.

Correct that F6 shows no chat, but that cuts both ways: with no rider message naming a route or stop, no consent under RD-5 exists in the record, and the driver's post-trip assertion of following the app route (F7) is a claim, not evidence — it happens to match F1.
Accepted: F5 itemises base $3.90, distance $11.99 (8.50 km), time $5.72 (22.0 min), $0.00 waiting and $1.47 platform to a $23.08 total with no unpublished add-on, so no FARE-1 refund line exists.
Agreed, and my C7 said the same: F13 shows 1 dispute with 0 upheld in 90 days, so RD-6's 'repeated' threshold is not met and no flag_account is sought.
Agreed on the substance: F1 shows 8.5 km actual against 8.5 km optimal (+0.0 km), so there is no unexempted segment and no distance refund under RD-1/RD-2. This confirms my D1.

Agreed: F3 confirms the billed 8.5 km does not exceed the optimal route and F5 shows the $11.99 distance component was charged on exactly that mileage, so nothing is refundable under RD-2. This confirms my D2/D7.

Agreed, and this is my own case: the +5.7 min in F2 went into the metered time component of $5.72 (F5), which on a RydeTAXI fare is chargeable by the meter, not an excess item under RD-2. This confirms my D3.

Agreed as to the records: F8 and F9 put both PIE and Airport Boulevard at band 3 (20-29 km/h) across 17:09-17:47 and F11 records 18.5 mm of rain, while F10 shows no incident, so weather and congestion explain the running time (F2) rather than any route change. This confirms my D4/D5.

Agreed: F6 shows no in-app chat at all, so no rider consent to any deviation exists and no consent question needs deciding under RD-3/RD-5; the driver's statement in F7 that he followed the app route is consistent with F1. This confirms my D6.
Agreed: F5 itemises base $3.90, distance $11.99, time $5.72, platform $1.47 with waiting $0.00, and F4 shows surge 1.0x, so no undisclosed item exists to refund under FARE-1. This confirms my D7.

Agreed: F13 shows the driver at 1163 trips/90 d with 1 dispute and 0 upheld and F12 shows the rider with 0 disputes, so RD-6's 'repeated' basis for flag_account is absent, and nothing in F6/F7 reads as a threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation requiring escalation under SAFE-1/SAFE-2. This confirms my D8.
